name: José David Cabello
detail: Head of the tax authority (Seniat) in August 2018; said the tax reform of that month (VAT from 12% to 16%, higher financial transactions tax, advance payments) was aimed at "ricos" and special taxpayers. These are consumption, transaction and income measures, not a tax on net wealth.

name: Impuesto a las Grandes Transacciones Financieras (IGTF)
detail: Tax on large financial transactions (the 2018 increase to 1%, later extended to payments in foreign currency); a transaction tax, not a wealth tax. Anyone who defends it is not recorded.

name: Partido Comunista de Venezuela (PCV)
detail: Its 2014 national conference proposed an "elevación del impuesto al capital" and a tax reform to make capitalists pay more; the text names no tax on net wealth, so it is not enough. It criticised the 2024 removal of the IGTF (a transaction tax).

name: José Guerra
detail: Economist, UCV professor and former deputy (Primero Justicia); criticized the proposed wealth tax on grandes patrimonios as having low yield and high collection cost compared to IVA/ISLR ('los otros son costosos y de bajo rendimiento').

name: Eduviges Morales V. / Mairely Hernández L. / María I. Delfín
detail: Authors of the 2015 ULA Actualidad Contable FACES paper analyzing a general wealth tax under constitutional principles; descriptive and critical academic analysis that does not endorse or recommend the tax (SKILL.md section 4: merely researching does not count).

name: Jesús Faría Tortosa
detail: Chair of the National Assembly economy commission; defended the IGTF (financial transactions) and the Ley de Coordinación y Armonización Tributaria (local taxes), both out of definition. No statement supporting the IGP or a wealth tax found.

name: Asdrúbal Oliveros
detail: Economist and director of Ecoanalítica; criticized the Impuesto a los Grandes Patrimonios as an excessive and distortive tax burden on formal private enterprise and advocated its elimination.

name: Ramón Lobo
detail: Economist, former finance minister and deputy; focused on price fixing (Plan 50), non-oil tax collection targets, IGTF, and municipal tax harmonization rather than net wealth taxation.

name: Julio Escalona
detail: Co-author of the June 2018 recommendations; obituary reports his death in August 2023.

name: Omar Galíndez
detail: 2018 co-author; a 2021 obituary by Alexis Corredor, a fellow co-author, identifies the academic as deceased.

name: David Nieves
detail: Named among signers of the 15 y Último version of the 2018 recommendation; the political leader died in 2021.

name: Vladimir Aguilar Castro
detail: Venezuelan professor and signatory of the July 2020 pact; memorial dated 27 September 2026 reports his death.

name: Eduardo Piñate
detail: The 30 October 2017 interview describes his committee considering eight executive bills, including a wealth tax. It does not establish his own support for that particular measure. Previously A0012 / E00014; reinstate only with individual evidence.
